$comment: The Cloud Logging retention this codebase PUBLISHES A PROMISE ABOUT.
web/app/politique-confidentialite/page.tsx tells users, in French and in
public: « Ces journaux ... sont supprimés automatiquement au bout de 30
jours. » That is a representation to users and to the app stores, not
documentation. Until 2026-08-22 the number behind it existed nowhere in this
repo — `_Default` appeared in exactly one prose sentence in ROADMAP.md — so
raising the bucket to 400 days would have left every check green while the
published sentence quietly became false.
Read in two directions, which is the point:
backend/test/infra/log_retention_test.dart  manifest <-> the published page
(offline, runs on every push)
infra/gcp/97-verify-log-retention.sh        manifest <-> the live bucket
(read-only, runs on the cron)
Neither alone is enough: the test cannot see GCP, and the script cannot see
whether anyone changed the sentence.
A PROPERTY, NOT A SNAPSHOT. `maxRetentionDays` is a CEILING, because the
promise is a maximum — 'deleted after 30 days'. A bucket set to 7 keeps the
promise (data is gone sooner); a bucket set to 400 breaks it. A checker that
demanded exact equality would fail on a change that is not a defect, and
would be turned off within a month.
NOT LOCKED, DELIBERATELY. GCP bucket locking is irreversible: there is no
--unlock, and the `unless it is empty` escape does not apply to _Default,
which Cloud Run streams into continuously. It could not be established that
locking even blocks retention INCREASES — the only direction that breaks this
promise — so it is an act that cannot be undone, cannot be rehearsed, and
whose protective effect is unverified. Watched drift is the honest trade.
NOTE FOR THE CHECKER: `describe` omits `locked` entirely when it is false.
The control is _Required, which GCP always locks and which does print
`locked: true`. Comparing a shell variable against the string 'false' passes
for the wrong reason.

backsPublishedClaim.why: the retention the privacy policy states to users
